post.caption: A lord wore gold and silver peanuts. In 1987, Walter Alva opened a Moche tomb in northern Peru. The mound, Huaca Rajada, stands near the village of Sipan. The lord was buried more than 1,700 years ago, with about 450 objects. Three pairs of gold and turquoise ear ornaments lay near his head, one pair showing warriors and another showing deer. Peanut shaped beads came in gold and silver, ten of each. The tomb also held a gold face mask and a crescent headdress. The finds are kept in the Royal Tombs of Sipan Museum in Lambayeque, which opened in 2002.
